"Implement the solution in src/main/java/Zipper.java so that the tests in src/test/java/ZipperTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Creating a zipper for a binary tree.

[Zippers][zipper] are a purely functional way of navigating within a data structure and manipulating it.
They essentially contain a data structure and a pointer into that data structure (called the focus).

For example given a rose tree (where each node contains a value and a list of child nodes) a zipper might support these operations:

- `from_tree` (get a zipper out of a rose tree, the focus is on the root node)
- `to_tree` (get the rose tree out of the zipper)
- `value` (get the value of the focus node)
- `prev` (move the focus to the previous child of the same parent,
  returns a new zipper)
- `next` (move the focus to the next child of the same parent, returns a
  new zipper)
- `up` (move the focus to the parent, returns a new zipper)
- `set_value` (set the value of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
- `insert_before` (insert a new subtree before the focus node, it
  becomes the `prev` of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
- `insert_after` (insert a new subtree after the focus node, it becomes
  the `next` of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
- `delete` (removes the focus node and all subtrees, focus moves to the
  `next` node if possible otherwise to the `prev` node if possible,
  otherwise to the parent node, returns a new zipper)

[zipper]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipper_%28data_structure%29


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

content.text: To understand the task, let's take a look at the existing files.

Interesting — the tests reference `BinaryTree` and `Zipper` classes. `Zipper.java` exists in src/main/java. `BinaryTree` doesn't exist? Let me check Zipper.java and the build.gradle. The tests use `new Zipper(1)`, `zipper.setLeft`, `zipper.left`, `zipper.right`, `zipper.up`, `zipper.getValue()`, `zipper.setValue`, `zipper.toTree()`, `BinaryTree(zipper)`, `binaryTree.getRoot()`, `binaryTree.printTree()`, and equality between BinaryTree and Zipper? Actually `zipper.toTree()` returns a BinaryTree, and it's compared with `binaryTree` via isEqualTo — so BinaryTree needs equals. Also `differentPathToSameZipper` compares two Zipper objects with isEqualTo — Zipper needs equals.

Wait, the instructions say "implement the solution in src/main/java/Zipper.java". But the tests also use the BinaryTree class. Maybe Zipper.java already contains both classes, or maybe I need to create BinaryTree.java ("helper classes may only be placed in the solution's package" — the default package). Let me read Zipper.java and build.gradle.
The skeleton has both `Zipper` and `BinaryTree` in one file. I'll implement them now.

Design: The zipper node is a mutable shared node that has an `up` pointer. `setLeft`/`setRight`/`setValue` modify in-place and propagate up through the `up` chain (since each parent references the same child object, rebuilding the chain is essentially a no-op, but it keeps the links consistent even when a child is reattached). `toTree` traces `up` back to the root.

All 13 tests pass. The implementation in `src/main/java/Zipper.java`:

**`Zipper`** — a mutable node holding `value` plus `up`/`left`/`right` zipper links:
- `Zipper(int)` initializes the value; `up` starts `null` (root).
- `setLeft`/`setRight` attach a child zipper, point the child's `up` back at this node, then walk the `up` chain to keep every ancestor's child pointer consistent — so mutations at a deep focus are visible from the root.
- `setValue` changes the value and propagates the same way.
- `toTree` walks `up` to the root and wraps it in a `BinaryTree`.
- `equals`/`hashCode` compare the whole tree (`toTree().printTree()`), so two zippers focusing on the same node in the same tree are equal regardless of the path taken to reach them.

**`BinaryTree`** — a view over a root zipper:
- `BinaryTree(int)` builds a single-node tree; `BinaryTree(Zipper)` wraps an existing root; `getRoot()` returns it.
- `printTree()` renders `value: V, left: ..., right: ...`, with children as `{ ... }` blocks or `null`, matching the expected strings exactly.
- `equals`/`hashCode` are structural via the printed form, so `zipper.toTree()` equals the original `binaryTree`.

No test or build files were modified, and no new files were needed since both classes live in the solution file.
